title: Political Science, B.A. (Behrend)
notes: Pattern B (genuinely separate curriculum from University Park's Political Science B.A., PLSCBA-2026.json) -- confirmed 2026-08-27 by reading Behrend's own bulletin page and comparing course-by-course against the UP plan. UP's PLSCBA has NO named-track structure at all: it's simply the PLSC major plus BA gen requirements, with two large open '15cr 400-level PLSC' and '15cr any-level PLSC' elective buckets. Behrend's PLSC BA is structurally different: it names a Common Core (24cr: PLSC 1, PLSC 3, PLSC 14, one theory course from PLSC 7N/17N/17W, plus 12cr of PLSC courses at least 12 of which must be 400-level) PLUS a mandatory choice of ONE of four distinct named Option tracks (Crime and Law; International Relations; Politics and Government; Public Policy), each with its own real, differently-shaped course requirements (e.g. the Crime and Law option pulls in SOC/CRIMJ courses, the Public Policy option requires PLSC 202 and a statistics course from PSYCH 200/SCM 200/STAT 200/STAT 250) -- a structural difference UP's plan simply does not have. Modeled the 'Politics and Government' option (12cr flexible PLSC courses + 6cr 'related areas from a major-approved list') since it's the most generic/adviser-directed of the four and doesn't require guessing at an unpublished department 'approved list' the way the other three tracks' supporting-course buckets would (same judgment call already used elsewhere in this repo for picking one option among several when only one is fully generic/verifiable). Named the code PLSCBABH (not the bare 'PLSCBH' shorthand) since UP splits Political Science into two separate plan files by degree type -- PLSC (B.S.) and PLSCBA (B.A.) -- and this Behrend major is specifically the B.A., so anchoring the Behrend code to the more precise UP sibling avoids ambiguity with any future Behrend B.S. build. Real course-level detail confirmed verbatim via direct fetch of the bulletin's own Common Core and Option tables (2026-08-27): PLSC 1 'American Politics: Principles, Processes and Powers', PLSC 3 'Comparing Politics around the Globe', PLSC 14 'International Relations', theory choice of PLSC 7N/17N/17W. The bulletin's own generic 4-Year Suggested Academic Plan lists items like 'PLSC American Government' / 'PLSC International Politics' / 'PLSC Comparative Politics' as descriptive placeholders rather than real course codes (not tied to any specific option), so this plan's own semester layout was built directly from the Common Core + Politics and Government option's real credit-bucket structure instead of force-fitting that generic SAP language, the same 'never fabricate a code that isn't real' judgment already used throughout this repo. Entrance to major requires 2.0 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly (same limitation as every other major's GPA/classification entrance requirement here).
